A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VPO research. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching despite added sections and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-bandit simulations, ARC-Challenge accuracy experiments and TL;DR preference evaluations in Sections 4.1–4.2 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations and LLM experiments in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: The value-incentivized objective, Algorithms 1–2 and experimental calibration policies are retained. The new Section 4 explicitly presents a token-level interpretation without algorithmic modifications.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic ten-arm bandit, offline ARC-Challenge multiple-choice task and online TL;DR summarization task. The new token-level formulation introduces no evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Both compare against MLE-MAB in the synthetic experiments, DPO and IPO on ARC-Challenge, and online DPO and the SFT reference on TL;DR. Newly cited concurrent methods are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: The experimental sections and Appendix C retain the same models, preference construction, metrics and evaluation procedures, including 1,172 ARC-Challenge test questions and the reported 3,000-step offline and 5,000-step online training budgets.

E4.justification: The exploration-weight comparisons, offline sample-size analysis and training curves examining overoptimization are retained in Figures 1–3. Neither the main text nor the appendices add ablations, robustness tests or case studies.

E5.justification: Both report averaging the synthetic-bandit results over ten independent runs. Run-count and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, with no added confidence intervals, significance tests or LLM seed information.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 retain the same plotted results and findings. For example, Figure 3(b) reports VPO win rates of 44.67% and 44.98% against online DPO for alpha values 0.01 and 0.1 in both versions. The appendices add no results.

T1.justification: v3 adds a substantial formal treatment in Section 4: a deterministic token-level MDP, trajectory preference likelihood, soft value/Bellman identities, calibration Assumption 3 and the token-level VPO derivation in Equations 25–36. The original guarantees and Appendix A–B proofs remain substantively unchanged. New Equation 36 contains a reference-policy denominator inconsistent with Equation 32.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about unified optimism/pessimism, implicit reward modeling, theoretical rates and empirical effectiveness. The added centering phrase in contribution (ii) clarifies reward calibration already described in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly connects the sentence-level formulation to autoregressive token generation through a deterministic MDP interpretation. Existing explanations of exploration-induced oscillation and resistance to overoptimization, and future directions concerning alpha and the calibration policy, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same prompts, calibration distributions, hyperparameters, coefficient schedule, hardware allocations and training times. No implementation or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands positioning by acknowledging similar concurrent algorithms from Zhang et al., Xie et al. and Liu et al., relating them to calibration-policy choices and distinguishing their theoretical settings. v3 also discusses Bellman-consistent pessimism and token-level RLHF literature, and explicitly credits Liu et al. for the online proof approach.

P1.justification: v3 inserts a standalone Token-level VPO section before experiments and expands related work while preserving most existing prose and section order. Other edits include keywords, the revision date, small clarifications and typo corrections; there is no pervasive rewrite.

P2.justification: Existing figures and algorithm boxes are repositioned relative to surrounding text, and Equation 14 is no longer split across pages. Figures 1–3 retain their designs, axes, legends and substantive captions; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves conceptual completeness through the token-level derivation and provides clearer attribution and comparison with closely related concurrent work. These are useful refinements to the retained method, guarantees and empirical evidence. The benefit is tempered by Equation 36 using the negative-trajectory reference denominator in its positive-trajectory term, inconsistent with Equation 32. Because the intended expression is recoverable from the preceding derivation and unchanged core objective, this localized error does not outweigh the explanatory and positioning gains.
